sections.h2: Offices that handle your Hernando County tax bill
sections.html:
Hernando County divides tax duties among three elected officers. One values land and approves exemptions, one sends the bills and banks the payments, and one records deeds and holds tax deed auctions. Before a sale closes you will likely contact each of them.

Write to the tax collector at 20 N. Main Street, Room 112, Brooksville, FL 34601, or email tc@hernandocounty.us. Homestead filings, assessed values and mailing name or address updates go through the appraiser instead. The Hernando County Property Appraiser keeps offices in Brooksville and Spring Hill and posts a parcel search and a tax estimator online.

  • Property Appraiser: what the parcel is worth, who qualifies for an exemption, who is listed as owner.
  • Tax Collector: the bill itself, payments, the installment plan and the lien auction.
  • Clerk: deeds on record and tax deed auctions.

sections.h2: When is Hernando County property tax due?
sections.html:
Notices are mailed in November. The county takes payment up to March 31, and an account that is open when April 1 arrives is delinquent.

Pay in November and you keep 4 percent. Each later month takes off a point, through February, and in March you pay the full amount. A payment mailed in a discount month counts by its postmark. Online e-checks cost nothing on current or delinquent bills, while a card payment adds a fee of 2.5% or $2.75, whichever applies as the minimum, paid to an outside vendor.

Businesses and rental properties also owe tangible personal property tax on furniture, fixtures and equipment. That charge rides on the same bill and gets the same discounts. A $25,000 exemption is open to owners who file a return by April 1. A landlord selling a rental can ask whether such an account is tied to the address.

sections.h2: How does the Hernando County installment plan work?
sections.html:
Under the plan a bill is paid in four quarterly pieces, and each piece is accepted only in its own month. You can sign up beginning every November 1, with a cutoff of April 30. Enrollment is final once the June payment clears.

Hernando County Tax Collector installment schedule
Due dateDiscount
June 306%
July 31None, keeps you on the plan
September 304.5%
December 313%
March 31Final payment, no discount

If you miss an installment, it comes due along with the next one. Anything left owing on April 1 is delinquent and gets no discount. Leaving the plan forfeits the discounts as well. Section 197.222 is the statute that created it.

A separate route allows partial payments on the current year between November 1 and March 31. It needs a signed application, wipes out all discounts and permits five partial payments at most, with the rest due by March 31.

Homestead in Hernando County lowers the taxable value of your own residence by as much as $50,000. To qualify, you need to hold title and have made the house your permanent Florida home as of January 1 in the year of the application.

Filings being accepted now apply to tax year 2027, with a March 1, 2027 cutoff. A later filing is counted for 2028. Owners can file in person at an appraiser office, send paperwork by mail, or use the secure online portal. A statewide Save Our Homes cap limits annual increases in assessed value to 3 percent or the change in CPI, whichever is lower. The Florida Revenue chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026.

Your bill shows all exemptions combined as one dollar amount labeled Exemption. After a sale the appraiser removes the seller's exemption and cap beginning the following year, and the new owner must apply again.

sections.h2: Unpaid taxes and the certificate sale
sections.html:
Starting April 1, delinquent tax in Hernando County accrues 3% interest, is advertised in a local newspaper, and adds advertising and collection charges. At month's end in May the tax collector auctions the resulting tax certificates over the internet on LienHub. You can still pay through May 29.

  • Bids open at 18 percent interest and step down toward 0.25 percent.
  • Whoever wins pays the taxes and takes a first lien on the parcel.
  • The county itself takes any homestead parcel with a taxable amount under $250.00, as well as one in litigation.
  • A certificate lives seven years unless bankruptcy interrupts it.
  • Once two years pass, the holder can request a tax deed sale, and the clerk runs it.

Any payment method works on a delinquent bill, except that a parcel already in tax deed status requires certified funds. When a deed sale draws no bids, the land is put on the list of lands available for taxes, and the county has 90 days to buy it first.

sections.h2: Closing on a Hernando County sale
sections.html:
Tax owed by the seller comes out of the sale proceeds at closing, and the recorded deed is what sends future bills to the buyer. After a completed deed reaches the clerk, the appraiser updates the roll's owner name. The collector's file catches up once the certified tax roll arrives in October.

On a deed, Florida charges documentary stamp tax at 70 cents per $100 of the price everywhere except Miami-Dade. Everyone named on the deed shares liability. Your closing statement ought to divide this year's bill between the two sides. If a tangible personal property account appears on the bill, tell the title company.

Each taxing body sets its own millage. The collector lists the county commission, the City of Brooksville, the school board and the regional water district among them. A millage report goes up on the appraiser's site after the roll is finally certified. To find the rate for one parcel, look at the TRIM notice that arrives in August or call the tax collector.

A few ordinary steps help. Have the title company get a written payoff from the collector near the closing date, because balances move. Keep the parcel number and a copy of your deed within reach when you phone an office. Scan every tax year for a balance, not only this one. When back taxes or a certificate could stall a buyer who needs a mortgage, a cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so the title company can pay off the debt from your proceeds at the table.

To contest a value, file a DR-486 petition with the Value Adjustment Board through the clerk's office. You have 25 days from the appraiser's August TRIM mailing. A petition that arrives after the date printed on the notice is too late, so note when your envelope shows up.

When a homestead exemption, classification or deferral is turned down, a separate 30 day limit runs from the date the denial letter was sent. The board rules on value and exemptions and nothing else. Rates are decided at the September and October budget hearings of each taxing body. If you own a rental or agricultural parcel, ask the appraiser's office, whose site has pages on agricultural classification, mobile homes and tangible property, whether another filing applies.

Collect your evidence first: recent sales of similar homes, photos of condition problems and repair estimates. Appraiser staff can often fix an obvious mistake in square footage or exemption status without any hearing.

faqs.q: When does Hernando County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: On April 1. The county takes payment through the end of March, then the collector adds 3% interest plus advertising and collection fees.

faqs.q: What discount does Hernando County give for paying early?
faqs.a: Four percent for a November payment, then one point less each month through February. March has none, and a postmark fixes the payment date on current-year bills.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Hernando County tax bill by card?
faqs.a: Yes, for an outside vendor's fee of 2.5% or a $2.75 minimum. Online e-checks are free on current and delinquent bills, and tax deed payments must be in certified funds.

faqs.q: How do I apply for the Hernando County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: File with the property appraiser in person, by mail or through the online portal. The 2027 deadline is March 1, 2027, and the house must be your permanent home on January 1.

faqs.q: Who runs the Hernando County tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: The tax collector holds it each year at the end of May, on LienHub. Bidders register there, and parcels come up one after another by parcel number.
